explain: _crās_ = tomorrow. For -āre verbs the future adds -bō to the stem: _labōrā-bō_ = I will work.
distractors: _labōrō_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I work'. The future is _labōrābō_.
_labōrāvī_ is the past: 'Tomorrow I worked' makes no sense.
_labōrābis_ is the 'you' form: 'Tomorrow you will work'.

explain: _mox_ = soon. Verbs in -ere and -īre make the future with -am in the I-form: _ed-am_ = I will eat.
distractors: _edēs_ is the 'you' form: 'Soon you will eat'.

explain: _bibō_ is a 3rd-conjugation verb, so its future I-form ends in -am: _bibam_. The water is the object: _aquam_.
distractors: _bibō_ is the present: 'Soon I drink water'.
The thing drunk needs the accusative _aquam_.

explain: _dormiō_ is a 4th-conjugation verb: the future I-form is _dormiam_ (stem _dormi-_ + -am).
distractors: _dormiēs_ is the 'you' form: 'Tomorrow you will sleep'.

en: Tomorrow I will walk to the forum.
explain: _ambulābō_ = I will walk. _ad forum_ = to the forum (accusative after _ad_).
distractors: _ambulāvī_ is the past: 'Tomorrow I walked' makes no sense.
_ambulō_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I walk to the forum'.
_ad_ needs the accusative _forum_; _forō_ is the ablative.

en: Tomorrow I will read a book.
explain: _legō_ → _legam_ (future) and _lēgī_ (past). Three tenses, three different shapes of the I-form.
distractors: _legō_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I read a book'.
The thing read needs the accusative _librum_.

en: After the meal I will walk.
explain: _post_ ('after') takes the accusative: _post cibum_. The verb is in the future: _ambulābō_.
distractors: _ante_ = before: 'Before the meal I will walk'.
_ambulō_ is the present: 'After the meal I walk'.
_post_ needs the accusative _cibum_, not the nominative _cibus_.

en: Tomorrow I will be at home.
explain: The future of _sum_ is irregular: _erō_ ('I will be'), _eris_, _erit_. _domī_ = at home.
distractors: _sum_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I am at home'.
_fuī_ is the past: 'Tomorrow I was at home'.

explain: _eō_ (I go) has the future _ībō_. _domum_ is the destination, with no preposition.
distractors: _eō_ is the present: 'Soon I go home'.
_iī_ is the past: 'Soon I went home' makes no sense.
_domī_ = at home, but _ībō_ needs a destination: _domum_.

en: Tomorrow I will see my friend.
explain: _videō_ is a 2nd-conjugation verb, so its future adds -bō: _vidē-bō_.
distractors: _videō_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I see my friend'.
The friend is the object, so he needs the accusative _amīcum meum_.

explain: _nōn_ goes right before the verb it negates: _nōn labōrābō_ = I will not work.
distractors: _labōrō_ is the present: 'Tomorrow I don't work'.
_labōrāvī_ is the past: 'I did not work'.
_labōrābit_ is the 'he/she' form: 'Tomorrow he will not work'.
